decisions.executionNote: Raise and gently pitch both tools toward a downward approach; left will grasp the basket rim. Board appears to show the slim black remote.
Basket is moving into the right workspace, so switch to right-hand rim grasp; left prepares above the incoming black remote without crossing.
Track the right basket rim while finishing vertical tool alignment and descending. Move left above the remote's lane; keep both grippers open.
Seat and close right fingers around the moving basket rim. Left advances toward the remote lane but remains open until basket lifting is verified.
Lift the right-held basket 12 cm and check visual retention. Reposition the open left gripper toward the black remote farther left on the belt.
Basket visibly rose with the right gripper; raise slightly more and bring it inward. After left IK interruption, use small retreat/descent increments to align with the remote.
Keep the basket held aloft; shift it closer to center without crossing. Left appears to contact the belt/object, so lift clear and offset toward the visible remote before another descent.
The remote is visible close to the left fingers. Make a small forward alignment and shallow descent, then close while matching belt motion; right maintains the lifted basket.
Lift the closed left gripper to test remote retention, retreating slightly for clearance. Keep the raised basket firmly held and slightly more central.
Remote remained on the belt, so reopen left and reacquire farther along its motion. Approach lower for a firmer pinch while right keeps the basket suspended.
Lower the left fingers about 3 cm to the remote's sides, following belt motion, then close. Keep the basket lifted steadily.
Allow left closure to settle, then perform a 7 cm test lift and verify that the remote follows. Right keeps the basket suspended.
Remote visibly remains between the left fingers after lifting. Raise above basket-rim height and carry inward with both grips closed, keeping left in its workspace.
Remote slipped during transport. Reopen and approach its new position cautiously; aim for a centered grasp rather than the end. Basket remains held aloft.
Remote has landed near the front belt edge diagonally. Approach its center and turn the left jaws across its short axis; right holds the basket steady.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller yaw and translation increments. Center the open left tool over the remote resting at the front edge.
Remote center is now between the open jaws. Fine-center, lower 2.8 cm, and close around its middle while maintaining the raised basket.
Let the centered pinch settle before a slow 2 cm lift. Watch the remote relative to the fingers; keep the basket raised and stationary.
Remote did not rise with the closed jaws. Reopen and lower the fingers farther around its sides for a deeper pinch, with only a small centering correction.
Lift clear of contact and realign the jaw direction with the remote's current long axis. It rotated during the last approach, so recenter before descending again.
Remote moved during rotation, suggesting contact persisted. Lift the open tool straight up to clear it completely before another centered approach; basket remains raised.
With the tool clear, move over the remote center and rotate across its new nearly horizontal orientation. Keep altitude and the right basket grasp unchanged.
Intercept the remote as it travels toward center, descending with final yaw alignment. Shift the still-raised basket rightward slightly to keep clearance from the left approach.
Fine-center the left fingers across the remote, descend another 3.4 cm, and close with settling time. Keep left on the negative-x side and maintain the right basket hold.
Settle the deeper centered pinch, then slowly lift and retreat from beneath the basket. Check that the remote stays fixed between the left jaws; right remains closed.
Remote remains fixed between the jaws. Stop retreating near the board and lift vertically to clear the basket rim, keeping both grippers closed.
Lift tracking suggests obstruction near the board or basket. Carry the retained remote leftward with a small rise to clear both before continuing upward.
Use the latest orientation after the guard interruption. Slowly move left, upward, and away from the board while retaining the remote and holding the basket fixed.
Remote slipped free again. Reopen and clear it at altitude, rotate the jaws across its newly turned long axis, and center over the visible body rather than its end.
Use the wrist view to move the remote's middle into the grasp region at safe altitude, finishing jaw alignment before descending. Basket stays held aloft.
Remote is fully visible in the wrist view. Align with its diagonal long axis and descend toward a middle grasp, keeping both arms separated and the basket aloft.
Track the remote's changing orientation against the front edge, moving the left grasp region toward its middle with a shallow descent. Keep the raised basket fixed.
Translate toward the remote across the wrist image while maintaining yaw, bringing the tool back from the basket and down to grasp height. Left remains on its side.
Center and deepen the left pinch, then let closure settle. Move the suspended basket away to the right and forward to give the pickup a clear upward path.
Test the settled pinch by lifting upward and forward, away from the board rather than dragging past it. The basket now has clearance on the right.
Remote is retained after the test lift. Raise it clear of the rim before slowly bringing the suspended basket inward beneath it; maintain both closed grips.
Add clearance above the basket rim while easing the lifted basket leftward and back beneath the held remote. Keep motion slow to avoid another slip.
Hold the remote at the reachable lifted pose after IK rejection. Bring the basket beneath it with the right arm rather than extending the left farther upward.
Remote now projects out toward the front-left. Bring the lifted basket farther underneath and gently turn the closed left tool to orient the remote into its opening.
The remote is no longer fixed in the left jaws and may be beside the basket. Withdraw the open left tool for an unobstructed view while holding the basket suspended.
The guard rejected the withdrawal near the folded limit. Start with millimeter-scale motion, then gradually retreat left and down without changing elbow configuration.
Separate the arms and shift the still-lifted basket right to expose the belt where the remote fell. Left retreats open for a fresh, unobstructed grasp.
After the guard interruption, clear the left fingers from the basket with smaller leftward increments. Hold the right pose closed and reassess basket retention.
The basket follows the open left fingers, indicating rim contact. Lift the left tool straight up to disengage rather than pulling laterally; right remains closed at its observed pose.
Remote has progressed toward the right workspace. Prepare a basket handoff: approach its left rim with the left gripper while the right continues holding it lifted.
Center the left fingers on the basket rim visible in its wrist view, lower slightly, and close to establish the receiving grasp before releasing the right.
Basket drift shows the handoff did not retain it. Clear the left tool and reopen/reposition the right across the outer rim for a secure regrasp, correcting its accumulated tilt.
The right rim is now between the open fingers. Seat them 2 cm deeper and close with a dwell; keep the left clear to verify this basket grasp.
Test the regrasp with a 10 cm lift and slight forward clearance. Keep the left arm clear and inspect the belt for the remote as the basket rises.
Basket visibly follows the right lift. Move it aside in the right workspace to expose the remote, while the open left tool approaches the center-left lane at clearance height.
Move the basket back toward center-left with the left arm safely withdrawn. Plan a supported transfer to the left so the right can retrieve the remote from its current lane.
Remote is visible on the right in the wrist view. Move the basket toward center and down for a supported left-hand regrasp; keep the left tool clear above its side.
Basket is stable near center and remote is exposed on the right. Approach the left rim at the same fore-aft location as the holding right hand for a controlled transfer.
Center the left rim in the wrist grasp region and lower to the right hand's grip height. Close and settle the left grasp while the right continues supporting the basket.
Left fingers appear seated around the basket rim. Keep left closed while opening and lifting the right clear; verify basket retention before moving toward the exposed remote.
Basket is retained by the left after right withdrawal. Lift it farther and shift slightly left; approach the moving remote with the right, yawing the jaws across its long axis.
Track the right-lane remote into the wrist grasp region while finishing jaw alignment and descending. Left maintains the basket and adds a small lift margin.
Advance the right grasp region toward the remote's middle instead of its trailing end, matching belt travel and lowering gently. Left holds the basket stationary above the belt.
Remote's middle is centered between the right fingers. Seat another centimeter, close across its sides, and let the pinch settle while tracking the belt slightly.
Test the centered right grasp with a slow 7 cm lift and modest inward motion. Keep both grips closed and verify the remote remains fixed relative to the fingers.
Remote remains fixed in the centered right grasp. Lift and carry it inward, gradually rotating its long axis toward the basket's length while the left holds the basket steady.
Continue carrying the securely centered remote toward the basket above rim height, gently rotating it lengthwise. Keep the left basket hold fixed.
Finish lengthwise alignment and gain 3 cm of clearance while approaching the basket's right edge. Remote remains fixed in the right pinch; left holds the basket raised.
Move the lengthwise-held remote over the right half of the basket opening with small increments and rim clearance. Keep the left basket hold unchanged.
After the IK guard, use millimeter increments and a slight lowering to stay continuous. Shift the basket beneath the remote while bringing it just inside the right rim.
